subject.title: Feature: Session authentication PIN gate (framework-level tool blocking)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core-owned session authentication gate, or should this remain a plugin/API-extension pattern built on before_tool_call?
rationale: The request crosses config schema, secret handling, session persistence, reset semantics, transcript redaction, and fail-closed tool execution, so automation should not choose the security boundary or default behavior.

options.title: Design a core SecretRef-backed gate
options.body: Add the primitive only after specifying secret storage, trusted verification, reset behavior, transcript redaction, compatibility, and recovery UX.

options.title: Keep it plugin-owned
options.body: Treat the existing hook surface as the implementation route and extend or document plugin APIs only where deployments cannot safely build this outside core.

options.title: Defer session PIN gating
options.body: Keep current allowlists, approvals, sandboxing, and external-content wrapping as the supported mitigation until a broader step-up-auth design is chosen.

recommendation.title: Design a core SecretRef-backed gate
recommendation.body: Add the primitive only after specifying secret storage, trusted verification, reset behavior, transcript redaction, compatibility, and recovery UX.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the session-state/config surfaces and is already in the timeline context for this product/security decision.
